what: Where the value of every per-tick input field comes from. `ports_gate.py` reads this and refuses to run green while an in-scope field has no row.
scope: structs whose name ends in `Input` or `Measurements` under include/foc/core/**
parameter_scope: scalar `step()` parameters under include/foc/core/** whose *name* carries a unit suffix -- the suffix is how this tree says "physical quantity"; `dt_s` is the host clock, not a measurement

kinds.contract: a declared contract names the channel (`hal/...` a hardware port, `core/...` an injected instrument)
kinds.host: a C entry in foc_api.h hands it in
kinds.derived: the library computes it from other fields; the producer names the header that does
kinds.constant: a number off a datasheet or a tuned scale, not a measurement; no producer
kinds.unfed: the application measures it and this project offers no channel -- a debt, printed every run

fields.note: The three-phase sum, read by whatever bench the integrator injects. The bench is a structural requirement of the board check, so this one had a channel before the gate existed. Typed as `duck`: `Bench` is a template parameter `board_check.hpp` accepts, not a method any header declares, and a row that named it as a method would be claiming a function that does not exist.

Per-phase current-sense offset, from the bench's own zero-current capture. Typed as `duck`: `Bench` is a template parameter `board_check.hpp` accepts, not a method any header declares, and a row that named it as a method would be claiming a function that does not exist.

Which way each phase responded to a known voltage: that is wiring, and only a physical bench knows it. Typed as `duck`: `Bench` is a template parameter `board_check.hpp` accepts, not a method any header declares, and a row that named it as a method would be claiming a function that does not exist.

Measured current ripple at a known duty; the bench's scope or shunt. Typed as `duck`: `Bench` is a template parameter `board_check.hpp` accepts, not a method any header declares, and a row that named it as a method would be claiming a function that does not exist.

The value the check compares the measurement against, computed by the caller from L, R and the switching period. A reference number, not a measurement -- if this came from the bench the comparison would be tautological.

Dead-time volt-seconds, measured from the phase-voltage distortion. Typed as `duck`: `Bench` is a template parameter `board_check.hpp` accepts, not a method any header declares, and a row that named it as a method would be claiming a function that does not exist.

The commanded dead time scaled by V_bus and the PWM period: the caller knows its gate drive and the library cannot measure it. `foc_axis_deadtime_v` is the arithmetic, but the dead-time and switching numbers are the caller's.
Produced by the electrical alignment routine, then read back here to be compared against its limit.

The field this gate exists for: until 2026-11-12 the HAL had no temperature at all and every integrator wrote the same divider inversion. The contract landed in 8785ea7. Known limit, stated where it can be read: the contract exists and nothing assembles it into this struct yet -- that is the drive supervisor's job, and a green row here does not claim otherwise.
Electrical speed, for the flux-weakening guard.

parameters.note: Alignment is the routine that *measures* the offset, so the angle it reads is the sensor angle -- the one number it cannot compute and must be handed.
The same sensor angle, on the alignment that does nothing: the signature is kept identical so a drive can swap one for the other without touching the call site.
The chopper decides on the bus voltage every step, so it is on the same contract the modulator reads; a separate port would be a second chance for the two to disagree within one tick.

The case this axis was extended for: the limiter was written before anything in the tree could measure bus current. The channel is optional and lives on the DC-link object rather than in `hal::DcLink` (a link that cannot measure current must be able to say so rather than report zero), so the producer is the trait, not `voltage_v`.
The torque the outer loop already asked for. The compensator adds to it rather than replacing it, so both numbers exist in the caller at the same instant.
Measured speed: the sensor contract when there is one, otherwise the observer, which the caller already holds -- the compensator takes a number, not a source of truth.
The application's own reference, the same number it hands the axis through `foc_set_speed`. The compensator is a policy the caller drives; it does not own a profile.

No capture channel exists: the application times the pulse with a timer peripheral and hands the width in. Kept as a debt rather than a `contract` because writing a `hal/rc_capture.hpp` with nothing behind it would be the same green field this gate exists for.
The breakaway sequence decides when the rotor has moved on the speed it is told; the assembly passes the sensor velocity or the observer estimate from the same slot.
Open-loop startup ramps the commanded angle but still needs the measured one to know when the rotor has caught up.
